claim: Repeating a Llama-124M FineWeb run while changing only the initialisation seed or data-order seed produces a pairwise mean absolute loss-trajectory discrepancy of 1.11e-2 and 1.62e-2 nats respectively - an independent measured small-scale noise floor in the 0.01-nat range.
stance_target: the 3.5%-relative (approximately 0.1-nat) noise floor used to declare a 9B-token null uninterpretable
scope_conditions: Llama-124M on FineWeb with AdamW, batch 128, sequence length 1024; pairwise time-averaged mean absolute loss discrepancy over evaluation steps
quoted_support: For an internal calibration, we measure run-to-run variation in our most extensively tested configuration, Llama-124M trained on FineWeb. Repeating the same configuration while changing only the initialization seed or data-order seed yields variations of 1.11x10^-2 and 1.62x10^-2, respectively, under the same metric.

claim: There is no configuration-independent threshold for when two pretraining loss trajectories differ meaningfully, but LLM optimizer studies routinely treat 1e-2-scale loss differences as meaningful - which places the practical detection threshold at ~0.01 nats, not 0.1 nats.
stance_target: the claim that a 9B-token run is underpowered by 2-14x because deltas sit below a 3.5%-relative floor
scope_conditions: survey of optimizer/hyperparameter studies cited by the paper
quoted_support: There is no configuration-independent threshold for when two pretraining loss trajectories differ meaningfully. Nevertheless, recent LLM optimizer studies routinely use 10^-2-scale loss differences to distinguish optimizer and hyperparameter choices.

claim: ELR-collapse errors of 1.8e-3 to 2.6e-3 are 4.3-9.0x smaller than the seed-induced variation, which is the paper's evidence that seed noise dominates any architecture-level signal at this scale.
stance_target: the relative magnitude of architecture signal versus seed noise at 124M
scope_conditions: three ELR-matched Llama-124M runs with both seeds fixed
quoted_support: the three ELR-matched Llama-124M runs in Figures ... with both seeds fixed, have collapse errors of 1.8x10^-3, 2.5x10^-3, and 2.6x10^-3. Thus, even the largest collapse error is more than four times smaller than the lower stochastic-variation baseline; across the reported values, the difference is a factor of 4.3-9.0.
